comparisons.peer_topic: Data Center Segment Product Portfolio and Strategy
comparisons.peer_summary: The Data Center segment includes server-class CPUs, GPUs, AI accelerators, DPUs, FPGAs, SmartNICs, and Adaptive SoC products. The company leverages these technologies to address computational, visual data processing, and AI workload acceleration needs by enabling optimization of performance and power for diverse workloads.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Micron identify 'high-performance computing' and 'AI' as primary drivers for their respective data center product portfolios, though they supply different hardware components. Micron highlights DDR5 memory as essential for these workloads, stating it 'offers the critical improvements in bandwidth and power efficiency necessary to meet the growing needs of high-performance computing, AI, and data-intensive applications' (mu_2024_1_P007_S002). Similarly, AMD describes its Data Center segment's role in addressing 'computational, visual data processing and AI workload acceleration needs' by leveraging 'high performance, energy efficient, scalable and adaptable compute engines' (amd_2024_1_P016_S002; amd_2024_1_P016_S003). While Micron focuses on the memory layer (bandwidth/power efficiency for data), AMD focuses on the processing layer (compute engines), they share the specific business driver of serving high-performance AI and HPC data centers.

sentences.text: DDR5 is the fifth generation of this technology and offers the critical improvements in bandwidth and power efficiency necessary to meet the growing needs of high-performance computing, AI, and data-intensive applications.
We leverage our technology to address the computational, visual data processing and AI workload acceleration needs in the data center market.

Modern data centers require high performance, energy efficient, scalable and adaptable compute engines to meet the demand driven by the growing amount of data that needs to be stored, accessed, analyzed and managed.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company provides advanced technology and IP platforms for customers to design ASICs targeting AI, high-performance computing, and networking applications.
comparisons.comparison: Both Micron and Broadcom highlight 'high-performance computing' and 'AI' as target applications for their technology platforms. Micron's DDR5 technology is designed to meet the needs of 'high-performance computing, AI, and data-intensive applications' (mu_2024_1_P007_S002). Broadcom provides 'custom silicon solutions' including ASICs that specifically target 'AI and high-performance computing' applications (avgo_2024_1_P008_S005). Both disclosures define their core product value proposition around enabling these specific high-growth, compute-intensive workloads, although Micron provides the memory component and Broadcom provides the custom logic/ASIC IP.

sentences.text: DDR5 is the fifth generation of this technology and offers the critical improvements in bandwidth and power efficiency necessary to meet the growing needs of high-performance computing, AI, and data-intensive applications.

• Custom Silicon Solutions: We provide advanced technology and intellectual property ("IP") platforms for customers to design and develop application specific integrated circuits ("ASICs") targeting AI and high-performance computing, networking and storage applications. Our custom silicon provides the platform to integrate embedded logic, memory, serializer/deserializer ("SerDes") technology, IP cores and processor cores. ASICs are custom products built to individual customers specifications.

comparisons.peer_summary: Broadcom provides Ethernet NICs, switching, and routing products optimized for AI data centers and service provider networks, focusing on high capacity, low latency, and scalability.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies address infrastructure demands driven by AI data centers, but focus on different layers of the stack. Micron emphasizes 'DDR5' offering 'improved bandwidth and power efficiency' for 'data-intensive applications' (mu_2024_1_P007_S002), which relates to the data storage/access bottleneck. Broadcom explicitly addresses the 'connectivity bottlenecks in data centers, particularly in AI data centers where compute bandwidth and cluster sizes grow rapidly' through its 'Ethernet network interface card (NIC) and switching solution' (avgo_2024_1_P008_S003). While both cite AI-driven bandwidth demands, Micron's disclosure focuses on memory bandwidth/efficiency and Broadcom on network connectivity/switching.

sentences.text: DDR5 is the fifth generation of this technology and offers the critical improvements in bandwidth and power efficiency necessary to meet the growing needs of high-performance computing, AI, and data-intensive applications.

Our products offer an enhanced, open, standards-based Ethernet network interface card ("NIC") and switching solution to resolve connectivity bottlenecks in data centers, particularly in AI data centers where compute bandwidth and cluster sizes grow rapidly.

comparisons.peer_summary: The Intel Arc graphics family powers immersive games, creator applications, and AI workloads. In 2024, Intel launched the Arc B-Series based on Xe2 architecture, featuring second-generation Xe-cores that deliver 70% more performance per core and 50% better power efficiency than the Intel Arc A750.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies cite 'AI workloads' as a key market driver for their products. Micron states that DDR5 offers improvements necessary to meet the needs of 'AI... applications' (mu_2024_1_P007_S002). Intel states that its 'Intel Arc graphics family... offers modern GPU features to power immersive games, creator applications, and AI workloads' (intc_2024_1_P031_S007). Both disclosures identify AI as a specific application requiring their respective hardware technologies (memory for Micron, discrete GPU for Intel), although the specific technical solutions (bandwidth efficiency vs. compute graphics) differ.

sentences.text: DDR5 is the fifth generation of this technology and offers the critical improvements in bandwidth and power efficiency necessary to meet the growing needs of high-performance computing, AI, and data-intensive applications.

The Intel® Arc™ graphics family offers modern GPU features to power immersive games, creator applications, and AI workloads. In 2024, we launched the Intel Arc B-Series based on the latest Xe2 GPU architecture. The compute engine of the Intel Arc B-Series is our second-generation Xe-core, which delivers 70% more performance per core and is 50% more power efficient than the Intel Arc A750.

comparisons.peer_topic: Data Center Platform Overview and Focus
comparisons.peer_summary: The NVIDIA Data Center platform accelerates compute-intensive workloads like AI and HPC, offering better performance and power efficiency than CPU-only approaches, and is deployed in cloud, on-premises, and edge environments via systems, subsystems, modules, software, and services.
comparisons.comparison: Both Micron and NVIDIA explicitly link their product benefits to 'high-performance computing' and 'AI' workloads, emphasizing performance and power efficiency. Micron states DDR5 offers 'critical improvements in bandwidth and power efficiency necessary to meet the growing needs of high-performance computing, AI, and data-intensive applications' (mu_2024_1_P007_S002). NVIDIA states its Data Center platform is focused on 'accelerating the most compute-intensive workloads, such as AI... delivering significantly better performance and power efficiency relative to conventional CPU-only approaches' (nvda_2024_1_P017_S001). Both disclosures define their strategic focus on enabling high-performance AI/HPC through superior efficiency and performance metrics.

sentences.text: DDR5 is the fifth generation of this technology and offers the critical improvements in bandwidth and power efficiency necessary to meet the growing needs of high-performance computing, AI, and data-intensive applications.

The NVIDIA Data Center platform is focused on accelerating the most compute-intensive workloads, such as AI, data analytics, graphics and scientific computing, delivering significantly better performance and power efficiency relative to conventional CPU-only approaches.

comparisons.peer_topic: Processor architecture and AI Engine capabilities
comparisons.peer_summary: Qualcomm utilizes System-on-Chip architecture with heterogeneous computing, including Oryon and Kryo CPUs and Adreno GPUs, to enable high-performance, low-power computing. The Qualcomm AI Engine features dedicated hardware and the Hexagon NPU for high-performance on-device AI inference, supported by the AI Stack and AI Hub to simplify developer integration.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies describe technologies designed for 'high-performance' and 'AI' applications with a focus on efficiency. Micron highlights DDR5's 'improved speeds, power efficiency, and storage density' for 'high-performance computing, AI' (mu_2024_1_P007_S001; mu_2024_1_P007_S002). Qualcomm describes its SoC architecture using CPUs and specialized engines to 'enable high-performance and low-power computing' and its AI Engine for 'high-performance AI inference' (qcom_2024_1_P025_S003; qcom_2024_1_P026_S002). Both disclose a strategic focus on delivering high performance for AI/computing tasks while managing power efficiency.

sentences.text: Double Data Rate ("DDR"): DDR memory transfers data twice per clock cycle resulting in improved speeds, power efficiency, and storage density.

DDR5 is the fifth generation of this technology and offers the critical improvements in bandwidth and power efficiency necessary to meet the growing needs of high-performance computing, AI, and data-intensive applications.

We have developed System-on-Chip (SoC) architecture with heterogeneous computing features, which uses our central processing unit (CPU) and different types of specialized engines (graphics processing unit (GPU) and neural processing unit (NPU)) to enable high-performance and low-power computing and other optimization techniques.

Our Qualcomm® Hexagon™ NPU is a key processor in our AI Engine and is designed for sustained, high-performance AI inference, enabling leading on-device AI capabilities with very low power consumption.

comparisons.peer_topic: AI research focus and on-device capabilities
comparisons.peer_summary: The company conducts broad research and development across AI, including generative AI, with the goal of advancing core capabilities to run on-device and scaling them across industries, leveraging over a decade of investments focused on power efficiency and personalization.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies highlight 'AI' as a critical area of focus and market demand. Micron identifies 'AI' as a primary application for its DDR5 memory technology (mu_2024_1_P007_S002). Qualcomm describes conducting 'broad, leading research and development across AI, including generative AI' to advance capabilities (qcom_2024_1_P054_S001). While Micron's disclosure is product-specific (memory for AI workloads), Qualcomm's is broader, covering R&D strategy and on-device AI, but both confirm AI as a central business driver in their Item 1 disclosures.

We conduct broad, leading research and development across AI, including generative AI, from fundamental research to platform and applied research, with the goal of advancing AI core capabilities to run on-device, and scaling them across industries and use cases.
